overclaim.name: PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (KEGG: hsa04151)
overclaim.reason: AKT1 and PIK3CD are central to this pathway, and several cytokine receptors (IL7R, IL21R, IFNGR1, IFNAR2, CSF2RB, PRL) can activate PI3K-Akt signaling, linking multiple input genes.

overclaim.name: NF-kappa B signaling pathway (KEGG: hsa04064)
overclaim.reason: TRAF6, TRAF3, TAB2, CHUK, IRAK1, and MAP3K8 are key mediators in the NF-kappa B signaling pathway, which is activated downstream of TLRs and cytokine receptors.

overclaim.name: Regulation of Complement cascade
overclaim.reason: CFH, CFHR3, and A2M are regulators of the complement system, modulating its activation and preventing host tissue damage.

overclaim.name: Regulation of Complement cascade (Reactome: R-HSA-977606)
overclaim.reason: CFH, CFHR3, CFHR4, C4BPA, and SERPING1 are regulators of the complement system, modulating its activation and preventing host tissue damage.

overclaim.name: PI3K-Akt signaling pathway
overclaim.reason: ECM proteins and integrins activate PI3K-Akt signaling cascade.

overclaim.name: NKG2D signaling (Reactome: R-HSA-198933)
overclaim.reason: MICB and RAET1E are both ligands for the NKG2D receptor, which is important for NK cell activation and cytotoxicity.

conservative.name: Apoptosis (KEGG: hsa04210)
conservative.reason: Multiple genes from the set, including TNFRSF10B, TNFSF10, BID, CASP2, and MAPK8, are involved in the apoptosis pathway, mediating both extrinsic and intrinsic cell death signaling.

conservative.name: TNF signaling pathway (KEGG: hsa04668)
conservative.reason: Genes such as TNFRSF10B, TNFSF10, JUN, MAPK8, and CASP2 participate in the TNF signaling pathway, which regulates inflammation, apoptosis, and cell survival.

conservative.name: MAPK signaling pathway (KEGG: hsa04010)
conservative.reason: JUN and MAPK8 are key components of the MAPK signaling pathway, which transduces extracellular signals into cellular responses including apoptosis and stress responses.

conservative.name: Apoptosis (KEGG: hsa04210)
conservative.reason: Multiple genes from the input set, including CASP8, CASP10, CFLAR, TRADD, AKT1, and IKBKG, are key components of the apoptosis pathway, participating in both extrinsic and intrinsic apoptotic signaling.

conservative.name: Autophagy (Reactome: R-HSA-1632852)
conservative.reason: BECN1, BECN2, and AKT1 are involved in the regulation of autophagy, a conserved cellular degradation process, with BECN1 and BECN2 being core autophagy proteins and AKT1 acting as a regulator.

conservative.name: PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (KEGG: hsa04151)
conservative.reason: AKT1, PIK3CD, and MAPK1 are all central to the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway, which regulates cell survival, proliferation, and metabolism.

mixed.name: Intrinsic Pathway for Apoptosis (Reactome: R-HSA-109606)
mixed.reason: BID, CASP2, and MAPK8 are involved in the intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptosis pathway, mediating mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and caspase activation.

mixed.name: Chemokine signaling pathway (KEGG: hsa04062)
mixed.reason: Chemokines and their receptors, including CCL2, CXCL1, CXCL5, and downstream effectors like AKT3 and MAPK9, are involved in the chemokine signaling pathway, which regulates leukocyte migration and immune cell activation.

mixed.name: B cell receptor signaling pathway (KEGG: hsa04662)
mixed.reason: SYK, LYN, and TNFRSF13C are key components of the B cell receptor signaling pathway, which is essential for B cell activation and adaptive immunity.

mixed.name: Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (KEGG: hsa04620)
mixed.reason: Genes such as TICAM1, IRAK1, TAB3, CHUK, NFKBIA, and TNF participate in the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway, which is crucial for innate immune system activation.

mixed.name: B cell receptor signaling pathway (KEGG: hsa04662)
mixed.reason: SYK, BLNK, PLCG2, and PRKCB are all involved in the B cell receptor signaling pathway, which is essential for B cell activation and adaptive immunity.

mixed.name: DNA Damage Response (Reactome: R-HSA-73894)
mixed.reason: ATM, CHEK1, CHEK2, DDB2, and RRM2B participate in the detection and repair of DNA damage, including activation of checkpoints and repair mechanisms.
